items.title: Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) on consumer hardware (RTX 4090) at 100T/s
items.summary: The latest advancements allow the Qwen 3.8 Flash Next model to run on consumer-grade hardware, achieving unprecedented performance levels of 100T/s. This development is significant for developers looking to leverage powerful AI capabilities without the need for expensive infrastructure.

items.title: Homa: The End of TCP for AI Clusters [video]
items.summary: A new video discusses Homa, a protocol that aims to replace TCP in AI cluster environments, potentially enhancing data transfer efficiency. Developers and engineers should pay attention to this as it could reshape networking strategies in high-performance computing.

items.title: Improper redaction reveals Google Data Center water and electricity usage
items.summary: A report highlights serious concerns regarding data privacy and security after improper redaction exposed sensitive information about Google's data center resource usage. This incident underscores the importance of robust data handling practices for engineers and developers.

items.title: AI search for every photo and every frame of video on macOS
items.summary: A new open-source project enables AI-driven search capabilities for all photos and video frames on macOS, enhancing media organization and retrieval. This tool is particularly valuable for developers looking to integrate advanced search functionalities into their applications.

items.title: The work by Valve's Timur Kristóf on improving old AMD GPUs on Linux
items.summary: Valve's Timur Kristóf has made significant strides in enhancing the performance of older AMD GPUs on Linux, which could benefit a wide range of developers and gamers. This work exemplifies the ongoing commitment to open-source improvements in hardware compatibility.
